 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. SUNDERLAND have issued a statement confirming today's Premier League game against Leeds United is "currently scheduled to go ahead as planned".
 The North East has been battered by rain and strong winds over the course of the weekend as Storm Boelo has taken hold.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement With that in mind, the Black Cats are encouraging supporters to allow extra time for their journey to the Stadium of Light ahead of today's 4.30pm kick-off against Leeds.
 RECOMMENDED READING: 
 The Sunderland player whose 'show of character' has impressed Regis Le Bris

 The Met Office says Sunday will remain stormy, with gales affecting many areas and heavy showers expected but gradually fading as the day goes on, with some brighter and drier spells developing later.
 Sunderland said in a statement shortly before 12.30pm: "Despite the ongoing storm and adverse weather conditions, the Premier League fixture between Sunderland AFC and Leeds United at the Stadium of Light this afternoon is currently scheduled to go ahead as planned.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Supporters are encouraged to allow extra time for their journey, arrive early where possible, and take extra care when travelling to the stadium.
 "Supporters are advised to keep an eye on official Club channels for any further updates ahead of the fixture."
 Sunderland are in desperate need of a win against Leeds as Regis Le Bris' side look to climb off the bottom of the table.
